source.text: כְּרָפְאִ֣י לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְנִגְלָ֞ה עֲוֺ֤ן אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וְרָע֣וֹת שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י פָעֲל֖וּ שָׁ֑קֶר וְגַנָּ֣ב יָב֔וֹא פָּשַׁ֥ט גְּד֖וּד בַּחֽוּץ׃

records.literal_gloss: when I heal Israel, then is uncovered [the] iniquity of Ephraim and [the] evils of Samaria; for they practice falsehood, and a thief comes in; a band raids outside.

en.L: when I would heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered, and the evils of Samaria; \q for they practice falsehood; \q a thief comes in, \q a band [of raiders] strips [people] outside.
en.B: whenever I would heal Israel, Ephraim's guilt comes to light, and the wicked deeds of Samaria, \q for they deal in lies. \q Thieves break into houses; \q gangs of raiders rob in the streets.
en.R: whenever I want to heal Israel, the sins of Ephraim and the evil done in Samaria come out into the open. \q The people lie and cheat. \q Thieves break into houses, \q and gangs of robbers attack people in the streets.

es.L: cuando yo quisiera sanar a Israel, se descubre la iniquidad de Efraín y las maldades de Samaria; \q porque practican el engaño; \q el ladrón entra, \q una banda [de salteadores] despoja [a la gente] afuera.
es.B: cada vez que yo quería sanar a Israel, salía a la luz la culpa de Efraín y las maldades de Samaria, \q porque practican la mentira. \q Los ladrones entran en las casas; \q bandas de salteadores roban en las calles.
es.R: cada vez que quiero sanar a Israel, salen a la luz los pecados de Efraín y el mal que se hace en Samaria. \q La gente miente y engaña. \q Los ladrones entran en las casas, \q y bandas de asaltantes atacan a la gente en las calles.

decisions.choice: when I would heal Israel, their guilt is uncovered: the healing is blocked by what it brings to light
decisions.reason: The sentence begins at the end of 6:11. The people were sure the LORD would heal them (6:1), but whenever he sets out to do it, their sin comes into the open and stands in the way, as a wound cannot be dressed while it is still full of dirt. The verb "heal" ties the verse back to 5:13 and 6:1.

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Samaria: the northern kingdom and its capital
decisions.reason: Ephraim is the northern kingdom (see 4:17). Samaria was its capital city, built by King Omri (1 Kings 16:24), and it stands here for the court and its leaders.

decisions.choice: a thief comes in, a band raids outside: lawlessness everywhere
decisions.reason: The thief breaks into houses and the gang raids in the open, so there is no safety indoors or out. The verb used of the gang means to strip, as raiders strip their victims (Judges 9:33 uses it of an attack).

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R); [of raiders], [people] (L); into houses (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word for sin in the prophets. Literal brackets the words it needs to make sense of "a band strips outside"; Balanced and Readable say where the thieves break in and whom the raiders attack.

decisions.choice: the sentence begun in 6:11 continues with a lowercase "cuando" / "cada vez que"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs across the chapter break, as the English shows; Spanish keeps it as one sentence.

source.text: וּבַל־יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ לִלְבָבָ֔ם כָּל־רָעָתָ֖ם זָכָ֑רְתִּי עַתָּה֙ סְבָב֣וּם מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם נֶ֥גֶד פָּנַ֖י הָיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they say to their heart [that] all their evil I remember; now surround them their deeds; before my face they are.

en.L: And they do not say to their heart \q [that] I remember all their evil. \q Now their deeds surround them; \q they are before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face.
en.B: They never stop to think \q that I remember all their wickedness. \q Now their deeds hem them in; \q they are always in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.
en.R: They never stop to think \q that I remember all the evil things they do. \q Now the wrong things they have done are all around them, \q and I see them clearly.

es.L: Y no dicen en su corazón \q [que] yo recuerdo toda su maldad. \q Ahora sus obras los rodean; \q están delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro.
es.B: Nunca se detienen a pensar \q que yo recuerdo toda su maldad. \q Ahora sus obras los tienen cercados; \q están siempre ante {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vista.
es.R: Nunca se detienen a pensar \q que yo recuerdo todo el mal que hacen. \q Ahora lo malo que han hecho los rodea por todas partes, \q y yo lo veo claramente.

decisions.choice: say to their heart: think, consider
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the place of thinking. To "say to the heart" is to tell oneself, to stop and think. The people never stop to think that God sees and remembers what they do.

decisions.choice: their deeds surround them: their sins hem them in on every side
decisions.reason: Their evil deeds are pictured as enemies closing in, or as a crowd around them that they cannot get away from (compare Psalm 40:13). They also stand before God's face, in plain view: nothing is hidden from him.

decisions.choice: never stop to think (B, R); in my sight (B); I see them clearly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1). "Before my face" becomes "in my sight" and, at Readable, "I see them clearly".

records.literal_gloss: With their evil they make glad [the] king, and with their lies [the] officials.

en.L: With their evil they make [the] king glad, \q and with their lies [the] officials.
en.B: They delight the king with their wickedness, \q and the officials with their lies.
en.R: The evil they do pleases the king, \q and their lies please the officials.

es.L: Con su maldad alegran al rey, \q y con sus mentiras a los príncipes.
es.B: Con su maldad deleitan al rey, \q y con sus mentiras a los jefes.
es.R: El mal que hacen agrada al rey, \q y sus mentiras agradan a los dirigentes.

decisions.choice: the king and his officials amid plots at court
decisions.reason: Verses 3-7 describe the court of the northern kingdom in its last years, when one king after another was murdered by conspirators. Of the last six kings, four were killed by men who then took the throne: Zechariah, Shallum, Pekahiah and Pekah (2 Kings 15:10, 14, 25, 30). Hosea does not name which plot he has in mind, and he may be describing the pattern rather than one event.

decisions.choice: they please the king with evil: the plotters flatter the rulers they will later kill
decisions.reason: "They" are the people of the court who plot (verses 6-7). Their wickedness and lies amuse the king and his officials, who do not see that they are being deceived. The king who enjoys evil will be destroyed by it.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The word for royal officers is "officials" at every level, as in Jeremiah. Literal brackets "the", which the Hebrew leaves out in this line of poetry.

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L); "jefes" (B); "dirigentes" (R)
decisions.reason: Sarim as the Spanish prophets have them, where the English has "officials"; the terms note keeps the Spanish words (uncertain).

source.text: כֻּלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים כְּמ֣וֹ תַנּ֔וּר בֹּעֵ֖רָה מֵֽאֹפֶ֑ה יִשְׁבּ֣וֹת מֵעִ֔יר מִלּ֥וּשׁ בָּצֵ֖ק עַד־חֻמְצָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: All of them [are] adulterers, like an oven burning from [the] baker; he ceases stirring, from kneading [the] dough until its leavening.

en.L: All of them [are] adulterers, \q like an oven heated by the baker, \q who stops stirring [the fire] \q from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
en.B: They are all adulterers; \q they are like an oven heated by the baker, \q who stops stirring up the fire \q from the time he kneads the dough until it has risen.
en.R: All of them are adulterers. \q They are like a hot oven, \q so hot that the baker does not need to stir the fire \q from the time he kneads the dough until it rises.

es.L: Todos ellos [son] adúlteros, \q como un horno calentado por el panadero, \q que deja de atizar [el fuego] \q desde que amasa la masa hasta que fermenta.
es.B: Todos son adúlteros; \q son como un horno calentado por el panadero, \q que deja de atizar el fuego \q desde que amasa la masa hasta que ha subido.
es.R: Todos ellos son adúlteros. \q Son como un horno caliente, \q tan caliente que el panadero no necesita atizar el fuego \q desde que amasa la masa hasta que sube.

decisions.choice: adulterers: unfaithful in marriage, and unfaithful to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word is used literally of adultery (4:13-14), and the prophets use it of Israel's unfaithfulness to the LORD (3:1; Jeremiah 9:1). Here both may be meant. The plotters at court are also faithless to their king, and their passions burn like an oven.

decisions.choice: the oven heated by the baker, who leaves the fire to burn low while the dough rises
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of the oven picture is hard, and the words can be joined in more than one way. The sense that fits verses 6-7 is this: a baker heats the oven, then stops tending the fire while the dough is kneaded and left to rise. The fire smolders through the night, and in the morning it blazes up. So the plotters' passion smolders, hidden, until the moment comes to strike.

decisions.choice: the oven: a clay oven heated from inside
decisions.reason: A household oven was a clay cylinder with a fire inside it; flat bread was baked against its hot walls. The fire could be left to burn low for hours and then stirred up again.

decisions.choice: they are like an oven (B); so hot that the baker does not need to stir the fire (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "they are" to join the people to the picture. Readable says why the baker can stop stirring the fire: the oven is hot enough already. That is the likely sense (m2), not certain.

source.text: י֣וֹם מַלְכֵּ֔נוּ הֶחֱל֥וּ שָׂרִ֖ים חֲמַ֣ת מִיָּ֑יִן מָשַׁ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ אֶת־לֹצְצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [On the] day of our king made [him] sick [the] officials [with the] heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scoffers.

en.L: [On the] day of our king, \q the officials made [him] sick by the heat of wine; \q he stretched out his hand with mockers.
en.B: On our king's festival day \q the officials made him sick with the heat of wine, \q and he joined hands with mockers.
en.R: On the king's special day, \q the officials made him sick with strong wine, \q and the king joined in with the mockers.

es.L: [En el] día de nuestro rey, \q los príncipes [lo] enfermaron con el ardor del vino; \q él extendió su mano con los burladores.
es.B: En el día de fiesta de nuestro rey, \q los jefes lo enfermaron con el ardor del vino, \q y él se unió a los burladores.
es.R: En el día especial del rey, \q los dirigentes lo enfermaron con vino fuerte, \q y el rey se unió a los burladores.

decisions.choice: the day of our king: a royal feast day
decisions.reason: The day may be a coronation, a birthday or another feast at court; the text does not say. "Our king" may be the words of the courtiers themselves.

decisions.choice: the officials made him sick with the heat of wine
alternatives: the officials became sick with the heat of wine
decisions.reason: The verb means "made sick", and the one made sick is not named; it is most likely the king, whom the officials get drunk. It can also be read "the officials became sick with the heat of wine". The word for "heat" can also mean poison (Deuteronomy 32:33). King Elah of Israel was murdered while drunk by one of his officers (1 Kings 16:9-10), and something like it may lie behind this verse.

decisions.choice: stretched out his hand with mockers: joined in with them
decisions.reason: To stretch out the hand with someone is to join with them, to make common cause with them. The king joins the company of mockers, the people who make fun of what is right (Psalm 1:1; Proverbs 1:22), not seeing that they are plotting against him.

decisions.choice: festival day (B); special day (R); strong wine (R); the king (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the day of our king" was (m1). Readable says "strong wine" for "the heat of wine" and names the king, where the Hebrew says "he".

source.text: כִּֽי־קֵרְב֧וּ כַתַּנּ֛וּר לִבָּ֖ם בְּאָרְבָּ֑ם כָּל־הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ יָשֵׁ֣ן אֹֽפֵהֶ֔ם בֹּ֕קֶר ה֥וּא בֹעֵ֖ר כְּאֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For they have brought near like the oven their heart in their lying in wait; all the night sleeps their baker; [in the] morning it burns like a fire of flame.

en.L: For they have brought their heart near like the oven in their lying in wait; \q all the night their baker sleeps; \q [in the] morning it burns like a flaming fire.
en.B: For their hearts are like an oven as they draw near with their schemes; \q all night long their baker sleeps; \q in the morning the oven blazes like a flaming fire.
en.R: Their hearts are like a hot oven as they make their secret plans. \q All night their baker sleeps. \q In the morning the fire blazes up into roaring flames.

es.L: Porque han acercado su corazón como un horno en sus emboscadas; \q toda la noche duerme su panadero; \q [por la] mañana arde como fuego llameante.
es.B: Porque su corazón es como un horno cuando se acercan con sus intrigas; \q toda la noche duerme su panadero; \q por la mañana el horno arde como fuego en llamas.
es.R: Su corazón es como un horno caliente mientras hacen sus planes secretos. \q Toda la noche duerme su panadero. \q Por la mañana el fuego se aviva en grandes llamas.

decisions.choice: their baker sleeps all night
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "their baker sleeps": the one who tends the fire leaves it to smolder overnight, as in verse 4. Some ancient translations, and many modern ones, read the same consonants with different vowels as "their anger sleeps" or "their anger smolders" all night. Both readings give the same picture of hidden passion that bursts into flame in the morning.

decisions.choice: in their lying in wait: as they plot an ambush
decisions.reason: The word is used of an ambush, of people hiding to attack (Jeremiah 9:7). The plotters come near the king with hearts burning like an oven, hiding their intent.

decisions.choice: in the morning it burns like a flaming fire: the plot breaks out
decisions.reason: The picture of verse 4 is completed: the fire left smoldering through the night blazes up at dawn. So the plot hidden at court bursts out in murder (verse 7). "It" is the oven, or the fire within it.

decisions.choice: as they draw near with their schemes (B); make their secret plans (R); the oven, the fire
decisions.reason: The Hebrew line is compressed: "they brought near like the oven their heart in their ambush". Balanced and Readable put it in order and name "the oven" or "the fire" for "it".

source.text: כֻּלָּ֤ם יֵחַ֨מּוּ֙ כַּתַּנּ֔וּר וְאָכְל֖וּ אֶת־שֹֽׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶ֣ם נָפָ֔לוּ אֵין־קֹרֵ֥א בָהֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: All of them are hot like the oven, and they devour their judges; all their kings have fallen; none calls among them to me.

en.L: All of them are hot like the oven, \q and they devour their judges; \q all their kings have fallen; \q there is none among them who calls to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: They are all as hot as an oven, \q and they consume their rulers. \q All their kings have fallen, \q and not one of them calls on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: All of them are as hot as an oven, \q and they destroy their leaders. \q All their kings have been killed, \q and not one of them asks {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help.

es.L: Todos ellos se calientan como el horno, \q y devoran a sus jueces; \q todos sus reyes han caído; \q no hay entre ellos quien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} invoque.
es.B: Todos están tan calientes como un horno, \q y consumen a sus gobernantes. \q Todos sus reyes han caído, \q y ni uno de ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} invoca.
es.R: Todos ellos están tan calientes como un horno, \q y destruyen a sus dirigentes. \q Todos sus reyes han sido asesinados, \q y ni uno de ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pide ayuda.

decisions.choice: their judges: their rulers
decisions.reason: The word means those who rule and give judgment, here the leaders of the kingdom, alongside the kings.

decisions.choice: all their kings have fallen: killed by plotters
decisions.reason: "Fallen" here means killed. One king after another was murdered in the northern kingdom (see the note at verse 3; 2 Kings 15:10-30).

decisions.choice: none of them calls to me
decisions.reason: In all the turmoil no one, king or plotter, calls on the LORD for help. They call on Egypt instead (verse 11).

decisions.choice: rulers, consume (B); destroy their leaders (R); have been killed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "rulers" for "judges" (m1). Readable says "destroy" for "devour" and "have been killed" for "have fallen" (m2).

source.text: אֶפְרַ֕יִם בָּעַמִּ֖ים ה֣וּא יִתְבּוֹלָ֑ל אֶפְרַ֛יִם הָיָ֥ה עֻגָ֖ה בְּלִ֥י הֲפוּכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Ephraim among the peoples he mixes himself; Ephraim has become a cake not turned.

en.L: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples; \q Ephraim has become a cake not turned.
en.B: Ephraim mixes himself with the nations; \q Ephraim is a flat loaf left unturned.
en.R: Ephraim mixes with the other nations. \q Ephraim is like a flat loaf that was never turned over, burned on one side and raw on the other.

es.L: Efraín se mezcla con los pueblos; \q Efraín es una torta a la que no se le dio la vuelta.
es.B: Efraín se mezcla con las naciones; \q Efraín es una torta que no se ha volteado.
es.R: Efraín se mezcla con las otras naciones. \q Efraín es como una torta que nunca se volteó, quemada por un lado y cruda por el otro.

decisions.choice: mixes himself among the peoples: mingles with the nations
decisions.reason: The verb is used of flour mixed with oil for an offering (Leviticus 2:4-5), so the baking picture of verses 4-7 continues. Ephraim has mixed with the nations through alliances, foreign gods and foreign ways, and lost what made it the LORD's people. Ephraim is the northern kingdom (see 4:17).

decisions.choice: a cake not turned: half-baked and useless
decisions.reason: A flat round loaf baked on hot stones or on the oven wall has to be turned. Left unturned, it is burned on one side and raw on the other, and no good to eat.

decisions.choice: burned on one side and raw on the other
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

source.text: אָכְל֤וּ זָרִים֙ כֹּח֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע גַּם־שֵׂיבָה֙ זָ֣רְקָה בּ֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Strangers devour his strength, and he does not know; also gray hair is sprinkled on him, and he does not know.

en.L: Strangers have devoured his strength, \q and he does not know [it]; \q also gray hair is sprinkled on him, \q and he does not know [it].
en.B: Foreigners have eaten up his strength, \q but he does not know it; \q gray hairs are scattered on his head, \q but he does not know it.
en.R: Foreign nations are eating up Ephraim's strength, \q but he does not realize it. \q His hair is turning gray, \q but he does not notice.

es.L: Extraños han devorado su fuerza, \q y él no [lo] sabe; \q también las canas se le han esparcido, \q y él no [lo] sabe.
es.B: Los extranjeros se han comido su fuerza, \q pero él no lo sabe; \q las canas se le esparcen por la cabeza, \q pero él no lo sabe.
es.R: Las naciones extranjeras se están comiendo la fuerza de Efraín, \q pero él no se da cuenta. \q Su pelo se está volviendo gris, \q pero él no lo nota.

decisions.choice: strangers devour his strength: foreign powers drain the land
decisions.reason: Foreign nations eat up Ephraim's strength through war and the tribute it has to pay them. King Menahem paid a thousand talents of silver to the king of Assyria (2 Kings 15:19-20), and King Hoshea paid tribute to Assyria too (2 Kings 17:3). The same word "strangers" returns in 8:7.

decisions.choice: gray hair is sprinkled on him: the signs of age and decline
decisions.reason: Ephraim is pictured as a man growing old without noticing it. The nation is getting weaker, and does not see it.

decisions.choice: Ephraim's strength (R); on his head (B); turning gray (R); realize, notice (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names Ephraim, where the Hebrew says "his", and varies "know" as "realize" and "notice". Balanced says where the gray hairs are.

source.text: וְעָנָ֥ה גְאֽוֹן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָנָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֨בוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א בִקְשֻׁ֖הוּ בְּכָל־זֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And testifies [the] pride of Israel to his face; and not they return to Yahweh their God, and not they seek him in all this.

en.L: And the pride of Israel testifies to his face; \q yet they do not return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, \q and they do not seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in all this.
en.B: Israel's pride testifies against him, \q yet they have not returned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God \q or sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in spite of all this.
en.R: Israel's pride is a witness against them. \q But even after all this, the people do not come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God \q or ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for help.

es.L: Y el orgullo de Israel testifica en su cara; \q pero no vuelven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios, \q ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscan con todo esto.
es.B: El orgullo de Israel testifica contra él, \q pero no han vuelto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios \q ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} han buscado a pesar de todo esto.
es.R: El orgullo de Israel es testigo contra ellos. \q Pero aun después de todo esto, el pueblo no regresa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios \q ni {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pide ayuda.

decisions.choice: the pride of Israel testifies against him: the words of 5:5
decisions.reason: The first line repeats 5:5 word for word. "Testify against" is the language of a witness in court; "to his face" means openly, in his presence. Israel's arrogance, its trust in its own strength and its alliances, is the evidence against it.

decisions.choice: pride: arrogance, self-reliance
decisions.reason: The word means height or majesty, and of people it often means arrogance (Isaiah 13:11; Amos 6:8). The pride is the attitude of verses 8-9, which does not see its own weakness.

decisions.choice: they do not return ... in spite of all this
decisions.reason: "Israel" is spoken of first as one person ("him") and then as the people ("they"). "All this" is everything the verses describe: plots, murdered kings, foreign masters and decline. None of it has brought them back to the LORD, though they had said, "Come, let us return" (6:1).

decisions.choice: shows clearly that he is guilty (R); the people (R); ask him for help (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pride testifies to, names "the people" for "they", and says "ask him for help" for "seek him".

decisions.choice: the first line worded as 5:5 at each level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 5:5 word for word, so each Spanish level repeats its own wording there.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם כְּיוֹנָ֥ה פוֹתָ֖ה אֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב מִצְרַ֥יִם קָרָ֖אוּ אַשּׁ֥וּר הָלָֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Ephraim has become like a dove, silly, without heart; Egypt they call, Assyria they go.

en.L: And Ephraim has become like a dove, \q silly, without heart; \q they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
en.B: Ephraim has become like a dove, \q easily fooled and without sense; \q they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
en.R: Ephraim is like a silly dove that does not think. \q The people call to Egypt for help, and they run to Assyria.

es.L: Y Efraín es como una paloma, \q ingenua, sin entendimiento; \q llaman a Egipto, van a Asiria.
es.B: Efraín se ha vuelto como una paloma, \q fácil de engañar y sin sentido; \q llaman a Egipto, acuden a Asiria.
es.R: Efraín es como una paloma tonta que no piensa. \q El pueblo llama a Egipto para pedir ayuda, y corre a Asiria.

decisions.choice: a silly dove without heart: easily fooled and without sense
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thinking (see verse 2), so "without heart" means without sense. A dove flutters this way and that and is easily caught in a net (verse 12).

decisions.choice: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria: Israel turns between the great powers
decisions.reason: In its last years the northern kingdom looked for help first from one great power and then from the other. Menahem paid Assyria to support him (2 Kings 15:19-20); Hoshea paid tribute to Assyria and then sent to the king of Egypt (2 Kings 17:3-4). Israel does not call on the LORD (verse 7).

decisions.choice: for help; run to
decisions.reason: Readable says why they call to Egypt and go to Assyria.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵלֵ֗כוּ אֶפְר֤וֹשׂ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ רִשְׁתִּ֔י כְּע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם אֽוֹרִידֵ֑ם אַיְסִרֵ֕ם כְּשֵׁ֖מַע לַעֲדָתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: As they go, I will spread over them my net; like birds of the heavens I will bring them down; I will discipline them according to [the] report to their congregation.

en.L: As they go, I will spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over them; \q like the birds of the heavens I will bring them down; \q I will discipline them \q according to the report to their congregation.
en.B: When they go, I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over them; \q I will bring them down like birds from the sky; \q I will discipline them \q as their assembly has been told.
en.R: As they go, I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over them. \q I will bring them down like birds out of the sky. \q I will punish them to correct them, \q just as they were warned.

es.L: Cuando vayan, tenderé sobre ellos {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} red; \q como a las aves de los cielos los haré caer; \q los corregiré \q conforme a lo anunciado a su asamblea.
es.B: Cuando vayan, echaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} red sobre ellos; \q los haré caer como a las aves del cielo; \q los corregiré \q como se le ha anunciado a su asamblea.
es.R: Cuando vayan, echaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} red sobre ellos. \q Los haré caer como a pájaros del cielo. \q Los castigaré para corregirlos, \q tal como se les advirtió.

decisions.choice: I will spread my net over them: the LORD himself will catch them
decisions.reason: The silly dove of verse 11 flies off to Egypt and Assyria, but the LORD is the fowler who throws a net over the birds and brings them down. They cannot escape him by flying from one power to another.

decisions.choice: discipline: correct by punishment
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a father who disciplines his son (Deuteronomy 8:5; Proverbs 19:18): punishment meant to correct.

decisions.choice: according to the report to their congregation: as they were warned
alternatives: because of their wickedness (a slight change to the Hebrew)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. It seems to mean "as was announced to their assembly": the warnings read out when the people gathered, such as the curses of the covenant (Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28), or the words of the prophets. The Greek translation reads the line differently. Some have suggested a small change that gives "because of their wickedness".

decisions.choice: from the sky (B, R); punish them to correct them (R); as they were warned (R)
decisions.reason: "Birds of the heavens" is "birds from the sky". Readable spells out what "discipline" means (m2) and gives the sense of the last line (m3).

source.text: א֤וֹי לָהֶם֙ כִּֽי־נָדְד֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נִּי שֹׁ֥ד לָהֶ֖ם כִּֽי־פָ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶפְדֵּ֔ם וְהֵ֕מָּה דִּבְּר֥וּ עָלַ֖י כְּזָבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to them, for they have strayed from me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against me! And I, I would redeem them, but they speak against me lies.

en.L: Woe to them, because they have strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q Destruction to them, because they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q And I would redeem them, \q but they speak lies against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Woe to them, for they have strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q Ruin to them, for they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q I would redeem them, \q but they tell lies about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: How terrible it will be for them, because they have wandered away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q They will be destroyed, because they have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I wanted to rescue them, \q but they tell lies about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: ¡Ay de ellos, porque se han alejado de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! \q ¡Destrucción para ellos, porque se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! \q Yo los redimiría, \q pero ellos dicen mentiras contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: ¡Ay de ellos, porque se han apartado de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! \q ¡Ruina para ellos, porque se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! \q Yo los redimiría, \q pero ellos dicen mentiras de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para ellos, porque se han alejado de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! \q Serán destruidos, porque se han puesto en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Yo quería rescatarlos, \q pero ellos dicen mentiras de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

decisions.choice: strayed: fled or wandered away, like a bird from its nest
decisions.reason: The verb is used of birds that flee or flutter away (Isaiah 16:2; Proverbs 27:8), so the picture of the dove (verses 11-12) goes on.

decisions.choice: I would redeem them: the LORD wanted to set them free
decisions.reason: "I" is stressed. The verb form can describe what the LORD wants to do ("I would redeem them"), what he did in the past, as when he redeemed Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8), or it can be a question: "Should I redeem them, when they speak lies against me?" The first fits the contrast with "but they".

decisions.choice: they speak lies against me
decisions.reason: The lies may be the false things they say about the LORD, such as that the Baals give the grain and wine (2:7, 10), or prayers that are not meant (verse 14; 6:1-3).

decisions.choice: Woe to them (L, B); How terrible it will be for them (R); rescue (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for a cry of woe in the prophets. Readable says "rescue" for "redeem", which here means to set free, as a slave is set free by payment.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay de ellos!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible será para ellos!" (R)
decisions.reason: 'Oy aimed at others follows Isaiah's hoy, as the terms note sets; "redimir" (L, B) and "rescatar" (R) as the Spanish prophets have the verb.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־זָעֲק֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בְּלִבָּ֔ם כִּ֥י יְיֵלִ֖ילוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם עַל־דָּגָ֧ן וְתִיר֛וֹשׁ יִתְגּוֹרָ֖רוּ יָס֥וּרוּ בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they have cried to me with their heart, for they wail on their beds; for grain and new wine they assemble themselves; they turn aside against me.

en.L: And they have not cried to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their heart, \q but they wail on their beds; \q for grain and new wine they gather themselves together; they turn away against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: They do not cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the heart \q when they wail on their beds. \q They gather together for grain and new wine, and turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: They do not pray to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sincerely; \q they just lie on their beds and wail. \q They come together to ask for grain and new wine, and they turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y no han clamado a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} con su corazón, \q sino que gimen en sus camas; \q por el grano y el mosto se reúnen; se apartan contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: No claman a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} de corazón \q cuando gimen en sus camas. \q Se reúnen por el grano y el vino nuevo, y se apartan de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} oran con sinceridad; \q solo se echan en sus camas y gimen. \q Se juntan para pedir grano y vino nuevo, y se apartan de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

decisions.choice: cry to me with their heart: pray sincerely
decisions.reason: They cry out for help, but not from the heart; their prayers to the LORD are empty, like the words of 6:1-3 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: wailing on their beds for grain and new wine: rites for good harvests
decisions.reason: The people wail and lament, perhaps in rites meant to move a god of storm and harvest to send rain. The worshipers of Baal believed he gave grain and wine (2:7, 10). The prophets of Baal cut themselves and cried out to him (1 Kings 18:28).

decisions.choice: they gather together: the Hebrew text
alternatives: they gash themselves (the Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads a verb that means "they gather themselves together", presumably at the shrines. The Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts read a word that differs by one similar-looking letter: "they gash themselves", as worshipers did in mourning rites, which the law forbade (Deuteronomy 14:1; 1 Kings 18:28; Jeremiah 16:6). The translation follows the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: when they wail (B); they just lie on their beds and wail (R); turn away from me (B, R)
decisions.reason: The small word between the lines can mean "but" or "when"; Balanced takes "when". The last verb is literally "turn aside against me"; Balanced and Readable say "turn away from me". Readable adds "to ask for" to show why they gather.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י יִסַּ֔רְתִּי חִזַּ֖קְתִּי זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑ם וְאֵלַ֖י יְחַשְּׁבוּ־רָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, I trained, I strengthened their arms; yet against me they devise evil.

en.L: And I, I trained [them], \q I strengthened their arms; \q yet against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they devise evil.
en.B: I trained them and strengthened their arms, \q yet they plot evil against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I trained them and made them strong, \q but they make evil plans against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y yo, yo [los] adiestré, \q fortalecí sus brazos; \q pero contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} traman el mal.
es.B: Yo los adiestré y fortalecí sus brazos, \q pero ellos traman el mal contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Yo los entrené y los hice fuertes, \q pero ellos hacen planes malvados contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

decisions.choice: I trained them: taught and disciplined them
decisions.reason: The verb is the one translated "discipline" in verse 12. Here, beside "strengthened their arms", it means to train, as a father trains a son or a commander his soldiers.

decisions.choice: strengthened their arms: gave them strength and success in war
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength, especially in battle. The LORD had given the northern kingdom victories, as under Jeroboam II, when he saved Israel and restored its borders (2 Kings 14:25-27). They used that strength to plot against him.

decisions.choice: trained them (B, R); plot evil (B); make evil plans (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "them", which the Hebrew leaves implied. "Devise" is "plot" and "make plans".

source.text: יָשׁ֣וּבוּ׀לֹ֣א עָ֗ל הָיוּ֙ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּ֔ה יִפְּל֥וּ בַחֶ֛רֶב שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם מִזַּ֣עַם לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם ז֥וֹ לַעְגָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: They return, not upward; they are like a slack bow; their officials will fall by the sword from [the] insolence of their tongue; this [will be] their derision in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: They turn, [but] not upward; they are like a slack bow; \q their officials will fall by the sword because of the insolence of their tongue; \q this [will be] their mockery in the land of Egypt.
en.B: They turn, but not to the One above; they are like a bow that will not shoot true. \q Their officials will fall by the sword because of their insolent tongues. \q For this they will be laughed at in the land of Egypt.
en.R: They turn, but not to God above. They are like a bow that does not shoot straight. \q Their leaders will be killed in battle because of their proud words. \q And for this, people in Egypt will laugh at them.

es.L: Se vuelven, [pero] no hacia lo alto; son como un arco flojo; \q sus príncipes caerán a espada por la insolencia de su lengua; \q esto [será] su burla en la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Se vuelven, pero no hacia el Altísimo; son como un arco que no tira derecho. \q Sus jefes caerán a espada por su lengua insolente. \q Por esto se burlarán de ellos en la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: Se vuelven, pero no hacia Dios, que está en lo alto. Son como un arco que no dispara derecho. \q Sus dirigentes morirán en la batalla por sus palabras orgullosas. \q Y por esto la gente de Egipto se reirá de ellos.

decisions.choice: they turn, but not upward: not to God above
alternatives: they return, but not to the Most High
they turn to what is useless
decisions.reason: The word read as "upward" means height. It may stand for God on high, as "the Most High" in 11:7, so that the people turn, but not to God. The Hebrew is short and hard, and some read "they turn to what is useless", or another way. The general sense is that their turning is not a turning to the LORD.

decisions.choice: a slack bow: a bow that cannot be trusted
decisions.reason: A slack or faulty bow fails the archer and the arrow misses. Psalm 78:57 uses the same words of Israel's faithlessness.

decisions.choice: their mockery in the land of Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt was the power they had called on for help (verse 11). The ally they trusted will mock them when their leaders fall. The officials are punished for the insolence of their tongues, their arrogant talk against the LORD (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the One above (B); God above (R); shoot true, shoot straight; killed in battle (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that "upward" means God (m1), and explain the slack bow. Readable says "killed in battle" for "fall by the sword", and turns "their mockery" into a sentence.

decisions.choice: "no hacia el Altísimo"
alternatives: no hacia Aquel que está arriba
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "not upward" points to God above; Balanced names him with the published title "el Altísimo", where the English has "the One above".
